correctionCommit.message: fix: authenticate developer tool host context

finding.rootCause: The exported createToolHostContext accepted caller-supplied ToolProjectScope and trusted executor identities. Its unique-symbol brand proved only that the exported constructor was invoked, not that a factory host created or attested the authority.
finding.requiredClosure: Only a host-owned binding may produce a usable ToolHostContext; stale, mismatched, structurally forged, or caller-expanded authority must fail closed.

inheritedCandidateIdentity.disposition: Preserved and checkpointed; R2-G1 changed only the four scoped paths listed in affectedFiles.

authoritySources: Private WeakSet membership in src/orchestration/tooling/host-context.ts proves the context is a host-created object in this runtime.
ToolHostContext construction validates scope/task identity, task capabilities, agent task-type support, and registered executor IDs.
authorizeToolRequest compares the request and supplied AgentTask against the host snapshot before registry and operation authorization.
The immutable Tool Registry and REGISTERED_TOOL_EXECUTOR_IDS remain the only tool/operation/executor definitions.
AgentDefinition permissions and TaskGraph task permissions remain intersections; neither request input nor agent role labels can grant authority.
requestCannotOverride: task identity, task type, or status
network policy, mutation mode, or dependency authority

beforeAfterBehavior.contextConstructionBefore: Exported createToolHostContext accepted a caller-provided scope and trusted executor list; the symbol brand did not establish provenance.
beforeAfterBehavior.contextConstructionAfter: The internal host-context constructor validates canonical task/agent/scope identity, freezes all authority arrays, accepts only registered executor identities, and records the exact object in a private WeakSet. The tooling barrel does not export the constructor.
beforeAfterBehavior.authorizationBefore: A branded caller-constructed context could supply authority facts to the authorization path.
beforeAfterBehavior.authorizationAfter: Untrusted structural copies/lookalikes fail with HOST_CONTEXT_UNTRUSTED; trusted contexts must match request project/version/task, current AgentTask identity/capabilities/file scopes, and supplied AgentDefinition identity before operation authorization.
beforeAfterBehavior.agent: AgentDefinition.allowedTools and supportedTaskTypes are host-snapshotted and compared; a lead/reviewer definition cannot impersonate the implementation host context.
beforeAfterBehavior.task: Task ID, project/version, task type, file scopes, allowed tools, and derived/required capabilities are host-snapshotted and must match the current AgentTask.
beforeAfterBehavior.project: The request projectId, projectVersion, and taskId must match both the host context and its current project scope.
beforeAfterBehavior.projectVersion: A version mismatch remains PROJECT_SCOPE_INVALID and cannot be repaired through request input.
beforeAfterBehavior.capability: Operation requirements are checked against host-snapshotted task capabilities; request input cannot add a capability.
beforeAfterBehavior.fileScope: Source selectors remain inside the intersection of immutable host allowedFileScopes and host taskFileScopes.
beforeAfterBehavior.network: Arbitrary URLs remain rejected by input policy; registered external adapters remain the only network-capable integration boundary and return UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL data.
beforeAfterBehavior.mutation: Operation mutation mode still requires a current mutable workspace where applicable; no generic write/edit/delete or shell operation was added.
beforeAfterBehavior.dependency: Dependency materialization remains a registered host runtime operation under the existing Dependency Authority; package names and command arguments cannot be supplied through request input.
beforeAfterBehavior.currentness: Only ready/running tasks authorize; cancelled/stale task status remains TASK_NOT_CURRENT.
beforeAfterBehavior.cancellation: Controlled runtime operation cancellation remains owned by the existing GeneratedProjectRuntimeValidator and typed runtime operation boundary; R2-G1 does not widen it.

forgeryTests.case: Structural copy of a trusted context
forgeryTests.before: A unique-symbol copy could look branded at the type/shape boundary.
forgeryTests.after: Private WeakSet membership fails; authorization returns HOST_CONTEXT_UNTRUSTED.

forgeryTests.before: Caller-supplied scope and task facts were not bound by the old constructor.
forgeryTests.after: createHostToolContext throws because host task identity does not match current project scope.

forgeryTests.before: Existing scope validation denied the mismatch.
forgeryTests.after: The trusted host snapshot is checked first; mismatch remains PROJECT_SCOPE_INVALID.

forgeryTests.before: Agent allowed-tool authorization denied the lead definition for the implementation operation.
forgeryTests.after: Host agent identity mismatch denies with AGENT_TOOL_NOT_ALLOWED before operation authorization.

forgeryTests.case: Forged capability or command-like request input
forgeryTests.after: Input policy remains INPUT_NOT_ALLOWED; request data cannot become authority.
